text: Security owner (docs/architecture/08-security-and-identity.md, 06 req 60 [proposed]): please add an OQ-security-and-identity-<n> row. Today Forwarded wins whenever it has content. So a client behind a trusted proxy that manages only X-Forwarded-For (the ALB, Envoy, Caddy, Traefik and Go ReverseProxy defaults) sets source.ip outright with `Forwarded: for=10.0.0.5`. It can also collapse source.ip to the proxy with `Forwarded: proto=https` or `Forwarded: ,`. That contradicts 04 section 9 risk 8. Options: prefer the header each trusted proxy is known to manage (a per-prefix header setting), or prefer X-Forwarded-For. internal/clientaddr/doc.go now states the risk and tells operators to have such proxies remove or overwrite a client's Forwarded field.

04 spec owner (04 req 16): please confirm that LOCAL with a UDP or UNIX family byte should close the connection. The PROXY protocol v2 text says a receiver must accept LOCAL and ignore the family byte. WP-15 keeps the literal 04 wording (refuse) and cites it in a comment in proxyv2.go. If the owner prefers interop, the change is one line: skip the family check when the command is LOCAL.

WP-46 (gateway/upstream outgoing request build), as a note for the consumer: clientaddr.Rewrite now documents its preconditions and panics with "clientaddr: Rewrite called with a nil http.Header" on a nil header. Note that http.Header(nil).Clone() returns nil. Apply Rewrite once per attempt to a fresh clone of the client header, and only after removing hop-by-hop fields and the fields Connection lists. Rewrite is not idempotent: with a trusted peer, a second call appends the peer again.

WP-44 (gateway/listener), as a note for the consumer: ListenerOptions.Clock must track wall time, because the header deadline goes to net.Conn.SetReadDeadline. Tests should pass clock.Real() or a clocktest fake seeded from clock.Real().Now().

Architecture owner (spec ambiguity, finding 5): the 4x stop and the cost model conflict. 07 req 15/58, 03 req 25, 04 req 47, 05 req 47 and section 2 Message.Decoded ('ErrTooLarge past 4x the raw limit') set the oversize stop at 4 times the raw limit, measured in 'size of built Go values'. That size is 3.05x the raw bytes for orders.json, 10.4x for short-member objects, 16.5x for [0,0,...] and 21.3x for [{},{}...]. At 4x, a dense numeric body at about a quarter of maxRequestBodyBytes therefore gets 413 RZ-RT-003 (07 T8). jsonval now exports MaxCostPerByte = 33 (a proven bound: Cost <= 33 * len for any accepted input) and documents the ratios, but leaves the multiple to callers. Please decide the multiple (keep 4x and accept the rejections, or use MaxCostPerByte * raw limit, or another value) and record it in 2.16. WP-34 cel DecodeJSON, WP-51, WP-60, WP-64 and the gateway body decoded-value reservations must all use it.

Architecture 2.16 / WP-37 / WP-39 (finding 6): jsonval.AppendCanonicalNumber is now total over finite literals and idempotent. Integer literals beyond ±(2^53−1) are rounded through the double path, matching encoding/json/jsontext, so for example 11e17 canonicalizes to 1100000000000000000 and parses back to the same bytes. As a result: stage G (WP-37) must call jsonval.CheckNumber(lit) on authored literals to raise RZ-CFG-005 for out-of-range integer literals and overflowing literals (02 req 16, 02 test plan item 3); WP-39 can rely on idempotence for verification step 31(b); and the canonical decoder must not apply the integer range rule to canonical content (123456789012345680000 is a valid canonical literal). Please record this in 2.16.

Consumers of jsonval (WP-34, WP-47, WP-51, WP-60, WP-64): an *Object of more than 8 members now costs CostIndexEntry (48) per member for its name index, so for large objects the *Object form costs more than the MapObjects form. Reads of *Object (Get, Index, Has, All, At, Len) never write, so a decoded tree may be shared read-only across goroutines; mutation still needs exclusive access.

Architecture 1.2, gateway/executor row: add internal/clock (the executor times Filter calls through clock.Clock, per convention 4) and internal/telemetry/catalog (span attribute keys AttrOutcome, AttrFailureMode, AttrStateOp, AttrStateDuration, AttrStateBatch, the Ops() labels and log keys). Spec 06 rule 8 requires the rule-1 401 RZ-AUTH-001 to carry every auth-class Policy's WWW-Authenticate challenge, and the SPI has no way to obtain it. The executor defines an identical executor.Challenger, so it matches structurally. WP-47, WP-48 and WP-49 (or WP-06's helpers) must implement `Challenge()` on their auth Filters.

The executor already honors it through errors.As, and otherwise maps: EvalError to cel_error, statestore.Error to state_store, ErrBudget to buffer_budget, ErrTooLarge to too_large, a panic to internal, an invalid outcome to invalid_result, anything else to internal.

errcode or the failure table owner (WP-01/WP-30): no registered default code exists for a cannot decide without a Filter code (in M1, a recovered panic) in the auth, admission and cache classes. The executor uses RZ-AUTH-002 (401) for auth and RZ-RT-011 (503) for admission and cache, outside RZ-RT-011's registered meaning. It uses RZ-PLG-001 (status from RZ-RT-011/012) for custom. A registry row or table note should fix these.

WP-01 (internal/filter/filter.go, filter.Consumptive.Undo doc): change it to 'Undo returns local tokens when the batch ends before the member's round trip completes (a local deny or a closed failure by any member) or an earlier member denied'. The executor undoes pending members that come before a local denier in chain order. Their round trips are never sent. Spec 05 req 64 covers only the members after the deny. (Finding 8.)

Optional, telemetry owner (internal/telemetry/emit.Span): spec 03 req 43 asks for an 'event on ruralz.filter.<name>' for a Policy.spec.when error. emit.Span has no event method, so the executor puts the error on span attributes instead (ruralz.failure_mode and error.type). Finding 4 asks for one shared RFC 8785 encoder with WP-39. internal/jsonval (WP-02) already has AppendCanonicalNumber and CompareUTF16, but architecture 1.2 limits config/schemaidx to api/schema, config/diag and config/tree. Note for the WP-37 (config/defaults, config/convert) and WP-56 (config/validate) reviewers: architecture R-7 overrides 01 J 39's RZ-CFG-005 row ('filterClass only for plugin') and 01 note 9 (materialization for plugin only). The registry materializes filterClass on every Policy, so stages G and H must not reject a non-plugin Policy whose filterClass restates its registry class. Registry.CheckFilterClass is the only filterClass rule; its doc comment now says so.

Note for the WP-38 (precedence), WP-56 (validate) and WP-59 (authz.cel Factory) callers: Registry.Phases now fails with registry.ErrNoBodyOracle when an authz.cel Policy has a non-empty config.rule and the BodyOracle argument is nil. Pass the CEL compiler (*expr.Compiler, which implements ReferencesRequestBody) on every Phases call that can see authz.cel. Phases also now rejects a wrong-typed Attachment.Config for every Policy type and checks it before the scope rule. Pass hub.Resource.Config as stage G decoded it (the NewConfig pointer type), or nil.

Architecture 1.2 lets internal/routematch import only errcode, while spec 04 section 3 proposes MatchKey(*v1alpha1.RouteMatch). I followed the table: MatchKey takes routematch.Criteria, a field-for-field mirror of v1alpha1.RouteMatch (with PathCriteria, HeaderCriteria, GRPCCriteria and GraphQLCriteria), and WP-56 and WP-42 copy the fields. If the lead prefers the v1alpha1 signature, add pkg/config/v1alpha1 (also L0) to the routematch row and a thin wrapper can follow.

04 req 23 and architecture 3.4 step 4 name r.URL.EscapedPath() as the normalization input. On Go 1.27.1, EscapedPath() re-escapes the decoded Path when the raw path holds a byte net/url will not leave unescaped ('{', '|', '"', non-ASCII), so '/a%2Fb/{x}' becomes '/a/b/%7Bx%7D' and the encoded slash splits a segment. WP-66 (handler) should call routematch.NormalizePath(routematch.RequestPath(r.URL)), and WP-30 should amend the input wording. This is covered by TestRequestPath.

WP-66 (gateway/handler) and architecture 3.4 step 4: do not turn every NormalizePath error into a fixed 400 RZ-RT-017. Take the status and code from the error with errcode.CodeOf and errcode.Status: RZ-RT-017 (400) for errors matching routematch.ErrRejected, and RZ-RT-001 (404) for routematch.ErrAsteriskForm. Also answer CONNECT and HTTP/2 extended CONNECT with 404 RZ-RT-001 (04 req 22) before calling NormalizePath; a CONNECT reaches the handler with an empty path, which normalizes to "/" and would match a prefix "/" Route. Please update the architecture 3.4 step 4 text to match.

Lead / WP-30: the adopted OQ-security-and-identity-21 (a) wording in architecture 3.6 ("and raw control bytes") should read "raw or percent-encoded control bytes". That matches docs/architecture/03-data-plane.md "Compiled structure", docs/architecture/08-security-and-identity.md "Request hardening", the RZ-RT-017 row and 04 req 23 ("any other control byte"), and it is what NormalizePath now does. If the lead picks the raw-only reading instead, revert the single case in NormalizePath's escape switch (the line that returns RejectEncodedControlByte), its oracle line in referenceNormalize, and the encoded cases in path_test.go.

WP-42 (gateway/router): the router-level test that `OPTIONS *` is unmatched does not exercise the real path, because the Router never sees that request. The end-to-end check belongs at the handler (WP-66) or in the protocol suite (WP-82): an `OPTIONS *` request should get 404 RZ-RT-001.

Integration note for WP-20 (executor): spec 06 requirement 8 says every 401 carries WWW-Authenticate. `Decider.Undecided` returns CannotDecide with an explicit code (401 RZ-AUTH-002 for auth), so the cause still reaches logs and the span. The executor's closed-failure 401 for auth-class Policies should add the Policy's `Challenger.Challenge()`, as `authRule` already does for rule 1.

Integration note for WP-70 (compile) and WP-47/48/49 (auth Filters): `auth.AcquireIndex` expects `BuildEnv.Shared` to memoize per snapshot compile. Each auth Filter should implement `auth.IndexHolder` (`CredentialIndex()`) so its KeyIndex carries over, and must call `Index.Release()` once from `Close`. `snapshot.Consumers` and `BuildEnv.Consumers` should come from `identity.CompileBundle(b).Map()` so the index returns the same pointers.

WP-20 (executor) / lead, for spec 06 req 8: in internal/gateway/executor/cursor.go fail(), in the `ph.CanShortCircuit()` branch, when `!sentinel`, `p.Class == phase.ClassAuth` and `status == http.StatusUnauthorized`, set `Header: http.Header{"Www-Authenticate": {v}}` on the returned *filter.Response, where `v` comes from `p.Filter.(Challenger).Challenge()` and is non-empty. This is the same lookup authRule already does for rule 1. Add an executor test: an auth-class fake Challenger returning `filter.Undecided("RZ-AUTH-006", err)` must produce 401 RZ-AUTH-006 with the challenge, still count ruralz_filter_failures_total{mode=closed}, and add no header for an empty challenge (auth.mtls). auth.Decider.Undecided already documents that the executor supplies this header.

WP-01 owner / lead (filter.Identity.Principal doc comment) and WP-30 (docs/architecture/08), for spec 06 req 22: the principal is `consumer.name`; else `jwt:` + iss + `#` + sub, with `%` and `#` in iss percent-encoded as %25 and %23 so the encoding is one-to-one; that form applies only when sub is a non-empty string. Else it is `mtls:` + subject when the subject is non-empty; else `""`, meaning no partition key. Please update the Principal comment and the 06 req 22 row to say this, and record an OQ-security-and-identity row (the next free number, 32 at the time of writing): 'What partitions an unbound identity without a subject?' Options: (a) no principal, never cached (adopted in code); (b) fall back to client_id/azp for JWT and the URI SAN for mTLS (risk: an IdP that omits sub would merge all users of one client app).

WP-63 (Response Cache) and later the Semantic Cache owner, for spec 05 req 79: on a Route whose chain holds an auth-class Policy and with no config.key, a request whose identity has an empty Principal must bypass both cache lookup and cache store. It must not use "" as a partition: "" is not a key and would share entries across clients and issuers. The principal may also contain the percent-encoded iss form above; treat it as an opaque string and never rebuild it from iss and sub.

WP-28 (schema): add `+ruralz:minProperties=1` to JWTBinding.Claims and a minLength of 1 to JWTBinding.Subject, so the schema rejects a jwt entry that binds nothing. Until then identity.Check reports it as RZ-CFG-005 at spec.credentials.jwt[issuer=...].claims or .subject.

Lead (still open), for spec 06 req 21: add a by-name quota map to expr.Consumer, for example `QuotaByName map[string]v1alpha1.Quota`. Meanwhile WP-62 (quota), which may not import identity, can read a Consumer's quotas from the typed v1alpha1.Consumer in BuildEnv.Bundle, looked up by consumer name.

secret.Use (and hub.SecretUse) carry no source location, so RZ-CFG-026 diagnostics have a resource and key-aware path but no file:line:column (the text form prints "-"). Additive request: a `Location diag.Location` field on secret.Use, filled from the loader's source map, which the resolver would copy into each diagnostic.

Doc owner for docs/architecture/08-security-and-identity.md (WP-30): document the secret file mode rule next to Secrets rule 5. On Unix, a file that is writable by group or others is refused with RZ-CFG-026. No owner is checked by default; resolver.Config.FileOwners can restrict owners. No doc change is needed for absolute symlinks, because the code now follows rule 5 as written.

WP-14 (gateway/setting) and WP-76: optionally add a process setting for an owner allow-list that feeds resolver.Config.FileOwners. It is not required; with no setting, any owner is accepted. Coordinate with WP-95: Compose bind-mounted secrets now resolve whatever their host owner, but a group-writable file (mode 0664, the default on hosts with umask 002) is still refused, so the quickstart should create its secret files with mode 0644 or 0600.

WP-41 (State Store driver): use the same loopback rule as the resolver for the credentials check and for state_store_unauthenticated (spec 08 req 8). Loopback means localhost in any case, an IPv4 address in 127.0.0.0/8, or ::1. IPv4-mapped forms such as ::ffff:127.0.0.1 are not loopback, even though netip's IsLoopback counts them. Proposed as the shared rule.

No change to the WP-01 contract code is needed. Documentation request for the Lead or WP-30 (finding 4): Security and identity 'Secrets' rule 5 should document three rules, or record them in an OQ-security-and-identity row. (a) A secret file writable by group or others is refused with RZ-CFG-026. (b) Any file owner is accepted by default; Config.FileOwners opts in to an owner allow-list. (c) Absolute symbolic links are accepted when they resolve inside the root: reads go through os.Root, with a filepath.EvalSymlinks fallback for absolute links. Request for WP-95: add a chmod 0600 or 0644 note to the Compose quickstart, because hosts with umask 002 create 0664 files, which are refused.

expr.Route.Prepared and expr.Consumer.Prepared say they are filled by 'Compiler preparation', but expr.Compiler has no preparation method. celtypes exports PrepareRoute and PrepareConsumer, which cache the sorted label views. Those without it still work: labels are then sorted on each iteration. Proposal: WP-34 exposes them to the snapshot compiler (WP-70) through an expr.Compiler method, or the contract drops the field.

expr.JoinedHeader falls back to strings.EqualFold (Unicode folding) and, when several non-canonical keys fold to the same name, takes whichever the map iteration reaches first, so the result can vary between calls. celtypes folds ASCII only (field names are ASCII) and prefers the canonical key, then the smallest key, so it is deterministic as 03 req 6.3 requires. The two agree on canonical net/http maps (fuzz-tested). Consider aligning expr.JoinedHeader.

WP-34 (internal/cel validator): reject a checked-AST struct-construction node (celast.StructKind) whose type name passes celtypes.IsObjectType (for example `ruralz.Error{kind: "connect"}`, `.ruralz.Error{}`) as RZ-CFG-014, so such a Bundle fails at configuration time instead of failing every evaluation with ErrUnsupported (and the place's runtime-error rule, such as 500 RZ-RT-006). TestIsObjectType in internal/cel/celtypes/eval_test.go shows the AST walk: celast.PreOrderVisit over checked.NativeRep().Expr(), matching e.Kind() == celast.StructKind && celtypes.IsObjectType(e.AsStruct().TypeName()). The celtypes runtime guard in Provider.NewValue stays as defense in depth.

WP-34 (informational): a missing map key, whether the key is constant or computed (`request.headers[request.method]`), fails in cel-go's own attribute qualifier with the text "no such key: <key>", not through celtypes' ErrNoSuchKey. That text can contain request data, so the runtime-error mapping must classify by kind and must not copy cel-go error text into problem documents or logs.

GatewayTimer (spec 09 reqs 53-54, implements emit.Excluder) lives in internal/telemetry/aggregate because 2.7 is WP-09's scope. But gateway/exchange and gateway/handler may only import telemetry/emit (architecture 1.2), so they cannot construct one. Request: move the dependency-free GatewayTimer into internal/telemetry/emit (it needs only sync/atomic and time), or add telemetry/aggregate to those rows.

emit.Shape.Routes carries names only, with no per-Route cache attachment. Following spec 09 req 45 literally, every Route therefore gets ruralz_cache_requests_total label sets pre-created (5 series each), which also spend that family's 6,000-set budget. Request: an additive RouteShape (Name, Cache bool) so only cached Routes get cache label sets.

Producer release contract for WP-40. To get pooling, the OTLP exporter wrapper must call Producer.ReleaseResource(rm) after Export returns. The /metrics handler must call Producer.Release on the scopes its wrapped Producer returned during Gather. Data never released is simply abandoned after 30 s, so this is safe but loses pooling. Each result may be released at most once.

Architecture 1.2 lists only 'otel sdk/metric' as the third-party import for telemetry/aggregate. Building metricdata also requires go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute and go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/instrumentation, both in the otel modules of section 5 and allowed by depguard. Please add them to the row.

Catalog (WP-01): add a process log key for a metric family name, for example KeyMetric = "metric". The one-time DEBUG record for a dropped code label now carries only catalog.KeyCode and catalog.KeyReason (unregistered or table_full) and no longer names the family.

For the Observability owner (spec 09 test 46, req 9 risk 1), please add an OQ-observability row with these figures. With S=8 and 125,743 series, live heap is 33.3 MiB against the OBS model of about 22 MiB (8.3 MiB aggregates + 8.3 MiB collection + 5.4 MiB striping). The overrun is in the aggregates: 25.5 MiB, which includes the handles and plans of both bound Revisions and one attribute.Set per label set, against a modelled 13.7 MiB. The pooled collection is about 7.8 MiB, under the model. The heap does not grow with a fifth reader (33.64 vs 33.65 MiB).

Earlier WP-09 requests that are unchanged: an emit RouteShape with a Cache flag; the Producer.Release/ReleaseResource contract for WP-40; adding go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute and sdk/instrumentation to the telemetry/aggregate row in 1.2; a catalog-level Policy-type-to-family table.

For WP-40 (telemetry Runtime), not a contract change: tracing.Options takes the Counters (spans_total; spans_dropped for queue_full and export_error; traces_unsampled for rate_cap_root and rate_cap_parent) as emit.Counter handles. The Runtime should obtain them from aggregate.Registry.Counter(catalog.TelemetrySpansTotal) and the corresponding family and label calls, and pass Resource and OnExport. It installs and swaps the OTLP exporter with Tracer.SetExporter; nil stops span creation, and the previous exporter is returned for the Runtime to shut down within its 5 s bound. Tracer.Shutdown gives the bounded flush at Drain.

Optional, for a future emit revision: emit.Span has no rename or AddEvent. The server span is therefore renamed '<method> <route>' when SetAttr(catalog.AttrRoute, ...) is called on it, and the 'failureMode: closed ending adds a span event' part of the M3 onChunk span cannot be expressed through emit.Span. No M1 change is needed.
Optional: the catalog has no attribute key for the onChunk chunk count (M3). StartChunk is otherwise complete.

internal/telemetry/emit (WP-01): the comment on emit.Tracer.Decide says "it never allocates". Change it to "it allocates nothing except the combined value when a request carries several tracestate field lines that are valid together (one allocation)". RFC 9110 requires those lines to be combined, and Decision.TraceState is a single string, so the value cannot be kept without one allocation. Invalid client input now allocates nothing.

Spec 09 req 38, req 70 and test 44, and docs/architecture/10-observability.md (lead): add an OQ-observability-<n> Open questions row and adjust the BenchmarkSampledTrace15Spans gate (at most 60 allocations, at most 30 µs). The SDK floor is at least 4 allocations per span (newRecordingSpan, context.WithValue, the SetAttributes slice, the snapshot), which is 60 for 15 spans before any Ruralz code. Measured: 89 allocations, 42 to 63 µs on a shared 4-vCPU machine. The Ruralz share is 15 span wrappers, the server span's parent and context, the name concatenation, and the leg headers and Inject in the benchmark.

Optional, to narrow the allocation gap (internal/telemetry/emit, WP-01): add an emit.Span method such as SetRoute(route, spanName string), as spec 09 section 3 sketches, so the snapshot compiler can precompute "<method> <route>" per Route and End no longer concatenates the name on every request. Without that contract the name cannot be precomputed inside the tracing package.

No WP-01 change is needed for WP-11. The telemetry Runtime (WP-40) needs to know: emit.NodeMetrics has no handles for ruralz_telemetry_logs_total and ruralz_telemetry_logs_dropped_total, so WP-40 should read logsink.Sink.Stats() and accesslog.Writer.Stats() at collection time. If handles are preferred instead, the lead could add a Logs [2]struct{Produced Counter; Dropped [2]Counter} to emit.NodeMetrics between waves.

WP-40 wiring: use one Sink per process (logsink.New with Options.Access set to the accesslog.Writer and TraceContext taken from the tracing span context); run Sink.Run as the only stdout goroutine; call SetRevision after each swap and SetCredentialHeaders with each Revision's auth.api-key header names; implement logsink.Bridge over otelslog and accesslog.Bridge (event.name is accesslog.EventName; timestamp Start, observed timestamp Observed). The Exported.Dropped flag keeps each record counted as dropped at most once (09 req 65). At Drain, cancel Run, wait up to 5 s, then call Close on both.

Information for WP-66 only; no contract code change is needed. accesslog.Writer.Acquire now returns a record whose FailureModes is nil. The handler may append to it or assign its own reused per-request slice, because Submit copies the entries and never keeps the slice. Assigning a reused slice keeps the zero-allocation steady state for records with failure modes. WP-31 (owner of docs/architecture/10-observability.md) and lead (spec 09): please record a conflict for RuralzSeriesFolded. Spec 09 req 72 asks for the exact OBS expressions, says rare-event rules add `or (x > 0 unless x offset <window>)`, and with test 43 asks every rule to fire on an event recorded before the first scrape.
